posts.author: SirGamers
posts.body:
Hey y'all,
I'm trying to make my RPG Maker game work on Mac, but when I tested it on my friend's Mac, it said "The application 'Game' can't be opened" (Game is the name of the file).
I'm not sure what's going on, cause I don't have a Mac, I use Windows, but can anyone help?

posts.author: fizzly
posts.body: Not 100% sure, but I think you need to deploy for Mac on Mac. Not 100% sure, but had the same problems with my friend. He couldn't open my game deployed on windows (checked as "for mac").

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body: Did you check "MacOS" when deploying the project? If that doesn't work, as far as I know, you need to be on mac to make mac builds (Hence why nobody in their right mind wants to support it)

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
@SirGamers
The Windows File System is missing a special flag that only exists on the MacOS file system and that signals to the MacOS "This is an app inside a folder".
This flag cannot be added while the output folder is on a windows computer, and extremely difficult to add on a Mac.
However some people found a workaround - you need to zip it and upload it to itch.io declaring it an MacOS app there, then download it with a Mac from itch.io
If done  correctly that will set the flags as needed.
Unfortunately I never did that myself, so I can't tell you how it is done. But there should be some topics on the forum from the last two or three years that explain this.

posts.author: Norintha
posts.body:
Dig down in the security settings to run unsigned code, there is probably some command key combo to do it too.
Edit: It's in the Ctrl click menu for M1 macs for sure.

posts.author: zslucky
posts.body: I had a similar problem and the solution was to use a mac computer to deploy the mac version. You can try borrowing one from a friend or coworker.

posts.author: Norintha
posts.body: Or your playtester can just open it correctly. My win 10 box produces Mac builds that work just fine once the Mac person okays running the unsigned code.
